chunks: And from him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who married a woman and gave her her dowry, and she stipulated that she held the right of sexual intercourse and divorce. He said: "She contradicted the Sunnah and gave the right to one who is not its rightful owner."
He said: "So he ruled that upon the man is the provision (nafaqah), and in his hand are sexual intercourse and divorce, and that is the Sunnah."
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a wife stipulates she holds the right of divorce and consummation in the marriage contract?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the default legal structure of marriage by contrasting the wife's specific stipulation with the established Sunnah. He affirms that while the wife holds the right to initiate consummation, the authority of divorce (*talaq*) and financial provision (*nafaqah*) remain with the husband, thereby correcting the deviation from prophetic tradition.
